annotationRationale: Independent game probabilities multiply along each winning path, and disjoint path probabilities add. The resulting quadratic is solved and filtered using the probability range.
sourceMethod: Follows the official enumeration of WW, WLW, and LWW, followed by the quadratic formula. Explains why the winning paths are exhaustive and do not overlap.

review.mathCheck: The exhaustive, disjoint winning paths WW, WLW and LWW give probability \((4p-p^2)/3\). Equating this to \(1/2\) yields \(p=(4\pm\sqrt{10})/2\); only the minus root lies in \([0,1]\). Thus \(m+n=14\), choice E, agreeing with the key.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA solution 17: enumerate the same three winning paths, solve the quadratic and discard the inadmissible root. The stopping rule and calculations are fully explained at AMC 10 level.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed probability concepts and supporting algebra and probability-range concepts match the actual work. No material omission.
